We present a comprehensive computational and theoretical analysis of the Erd˝osSzemer´edi sunflower problem. We compute exact values m(n, 3) = 2, 4, 6, 9, 13, 20 for n = L6@P0: 1, . . . , 6—a sequence absent from the literature for the power-set formulation. Our central L7@P0: results establish proven slack in the Naslund-Sawin bound at multiple values: 41.7% at L8@P0: n = 3 and 4.5% at n = 6 (Theorem 4.3). We prove that each local “blocking” tensor has L9@P0: slice rank exactly 2, while the Naslund-Sawin proof implicitly uses factor 3—identifying the L10@P0: precise source of overcounting. We prove a Strong Balance Theorem: in any maximum L11@P0: sunflower-free family, element frequencies satisfy m(n, 3) − m(n − 1, 3) ≤ di ≤ m(n − 1, 3) − 1, L12@P0: implying frequencies lie in approximately [0.33, 0.67] (Theorem 5.5). These structural insights, L13@P0: combined with the observed monotonic decay of |Fmax|/NS(n) from 0.84 to 0.42, point to L14@P0: specific directions for asymptotic improvement.
